prompt:
Research the official rate limits of the public GitHub REST API for unauthenticated and authenticated requests. Cite the GitHub documentation page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official GitHub documentation, the rate limits for the public REST API differ significantly depending on whether the request is authenticated or unauthenticated.

**Unauthenticated Requests**
For users making requests without authentication (typically to fetch public data), the limit is quite low and is tied to the originating IP address rather than a specific user account.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "The primary rate limit for unauthenticated requests is 60 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 requests per hour.

**Authenticated Requests**
When using a personal access token, GitHub App, or OAuth app, the rate limit increases substantially. These requests count toward a personal hourly budget.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Authenticated users have a primary rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

However, there are exceptions for users within GitHub Enterprise Cloud organizations using specific apps.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "Requests made on your behalf by a GitHub App that is owned by a GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization have a higher rate limit of 15,000 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Authenticated requests made via GitHub Apps owned by GitHub Enterprise Cloud organizations have a limit of 15,000 requests per hour.

**Git LFS Rate Limits**
It is also important to note that Git Large File Storage (LFS) operations have a separate rate limiting bucket with much higher throughput, measured in requests per minute rather than per hour.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "These count towards a separate rate limiting bucket with a limit of 300 requests per minute for unauthenticated requests and 3,000 requests per minute for authenticated requests." | CLAIM: Git LFS API requests have separate limits of 300 requests per minute for unauthenticated users and 3,000 requests per minute for authenticated users.
